entries.author: Arx
entries.title: Qin's First Emperor Orders the Books Burned
entries.dek: In 213 BC the chancellor Li Si persuades the First Emperor to burn private copies of the Odes, the Documents and rival states' histories. Historians still argue over how much burned.

pair.left: Chunyu Yue said no state had lasted long without taking antiquity as its teacher, and urged the emperor to give fiefs to his sons and brothers.
pair.right: Li Si said times had changed, that scholars studied the past to criticize the present and confuse the people, and that their books should burn.

reading.label: The Stakes
reading.text: Each man said he was guarding the dynasty; at stake was who could judge the emperor's rule, scholars reading old books or officials teaching the new law.

entries.title: Moscow Gets a Patriarch and Calls Itself the Third Rome
entries.dek: In 1589 the patriarch of Constantinople installs Job as Moscow's first patriarch, in a charter that names Russia the Third Rome. In 2018 the two churches split over Kyiv.

pair.left: In 2018 Moscow's Holy Synod said Constantinople's Ukraine decisions were an "encroachment on someone else's canonical regions" and broke communion with it.
pair.right: In 2018 Constantinople's Holy Synod said the 1686 letter letting Moscow ordain Kyiv's metropolitan was "issued for the circumstances of that time" and revoked it.

reading.label: The Stakes
reading.text: Both churches cite old charters; at stake is who ranks first in Orthodoxy, and whether the church in Kyiv answers to Moscow or stands on its own.

entries.title: Crusaders Sack Béziers and the Cathar War Begins
entries.dek: On 22 July 1209 the army Innocent III raised against the Cathars storms Béziers and kills Catholics and heretics alike. Twenty years later Languedoc is bound to the French crown.

pair.left: The legate Arnaud Amalric told Innocent III that the crusaders spared no one in Béziers, put almost 20,000 to the sword, and that divine vengeance raged against the city.
pair.right: Raymond Roger Trencavel, viscount of Béziers, said he was a loyal member of the Church and, being young, not to blame for the heresy in his lands.

reading.label: The Stakes
reading.text: Each side said it stood with the Church; at stake was who would rule Languedoc and police its faith, the pope's legates and northern barons or the southern lords.
